_comment: End-to-end `bestiary series <selector>` resolution: the specificity ladder, the canonical grammar readings, --version, --input-format, and the disagreement errors. Each case drives run() and asserts the rendered line names (and, where the case is about a release-level cut, the release names per line). must-fail cases assert the error names what was wrong. See TESTING.md.

provenance.ref: specificity ladder rung 1: a family selector returns every generation of that family, including the un-versioned bare line

mutation.description: selector carries a family name and no version, so nothing narrows the generation

provenance.ref: user ruling verbatim: 'bestiary series claude-4 ... will return all in the 4.x series'

mutation.description: selector gains a bare-integer generation, narrowing the family rung to one major union

provenance.ref: user ruling verbatim: 'or bestiary series claude --version 4' — the same selection by another spelling

mutation.description: the generation moves from the selector string into --version; the result must not change

provenance.ref: user ruling verbatim: 'But more specific 4.8 or 4.0 will return the narrower specification'

mutation.description: the selector's generation gains a minor part, narrowing the union to the single line

provenance.ref: the second narrow example the user named alongside 4.0

mutation.description: a different minor of the same major must select only itself, proving the narrow rung is not aliased to the union

provenance.ref: --version must reach the narrow rung too, not only the major union

mutation.description: --version carries a dotted version, which must narrow rather than union

provenance.ref: regression guard: the family reading predates the version selectors and must be unchanged by them, including the bare gemma line whose rendering equals the family name

mutation.description: no version anywhere in the query, so only the pre-existing family reading may fire

provenance.ref: strict rule: a generation joins version 5 iff it IS 5 or begins '5.'; glm's 5p1/5p2 spellings are decoded at PARSE into 5.1/5.2 and join as ordinary dotted members, never by a p-aware selector

mutation.description: the union is taken over a family that also ships p-notation ids upstream; no 5pX generation may appear as a line. RE-MEASURED at the 2026-08-28 models.dev catalog refresh: the union gains `glm-5.3`, a NEW upstream GLM 5.3 line (entities glm@5.3 and glm/flash@5.3) spelled with an ordinary dot. It is not a p-notation row and it does not weaken the claim — the claim is that no `5pX` GENERATION may appear as a line, and none does

provenance.ref: gemini@001 is a real catalog generation spelling; '001' is not '1' and does not begin '1.', so the strict rule excludes it. RE-MEASURED at the 2026-08-28 models.dev catalog refresh: upstream retired the last Gemini 1.5 rows, so gemini has NO 1.x line left while `gemini-001` is still a live line. The case therefore flips from must-pass to must-fail, and the claim it makes gets STRONGER rather than weaker: `gemini-1` now finds nothing at all, which is only possible if the leading-zero generation `001` is excluded from the version-1 union. Under a numeric reading it would have been folded in and the selector would have answered. The expectation is not relaxed to a not-found to go green — a not-found IS the sharper proof of the exclusion, and the case fails loudly again the moment `gemini-001` starts answering to `gemini-1`

mutation.description: the union is taken over a family carrying a leading-zero generation and NO ordinary version-1 line, so the leading-zero spelling is the only thing a numeric normalization could return; it must not be normalized in, which makes the selector a not-found

provenance.ref: minimax@25 and minimax@27 are dot-lost upstream spellings; a bare-prefix rule would wrongly swallow them into version 2

mutation.description: the union is taken over a family carrying dot-lost generations, which the mandatory dot must exclude

provenance.ref: ruled: where a family spells BOTH a bare N line and N.x siblings, the union includes the bare line (21 such families in the catalog)

mutation.description: the union is taken over a family whose bare-N line survived the N->N.0 fold, so the bare line must be a member

provenance.ref: ruled: sub-1.0 lines union under version 0 verbatim; no exemption is needed because nothing folds

mutation.description: the version is 0, the one value whose union would need a special case if the rule were numeric rather than string-based. RE-MEASURED at the 2026-08-28 models.dev catalog refresh: upstream retired the mistral 0.1 rows and published a 0.2 line (mistral@0.2#7b{instruct}), so the members change while the RULE under test does not — two sub-1.0 lines still union verbatim under version 0

provenance.ref: ruled: a bare-integer selector that IS its own line returns that line, as before the version selectors existed

mutation.description: the union is taken over a family with no dotted siblings, so it must collapse to the single pre-existing line

provenance.ref: canonical grammar mapped to series meaning: '@' is the entity VERSION (as in an entity key), so claude@4 is the major-4 union

mutation.description: the generation is spelled with the canonical '@' instead of the ladder's '-'; the selection must be identical

provenance.ref: canonical grammar: a fully specified @version narrows exactly as the ladder's minor rung does

mutation.description: the canonical version gains a minor part, which must narrow rather than union

provenance.ref: new release-level cut: the opus release across ALL claude generations, each series showing only its opus release

mutation.description: a variant segment is added with no version, cutting every generation down to one release and dropping the lines that have no opus release. RE-MEASURED at the 2026-08-28 models.dev catalog refresh: the cut gains `claude-5`, Anthropic's new Claude 5 generation, which has an opus release (claude/opus@5). Lines without an opus release still drop out, which is what the cut asserts

provenance.ref: the release cut composed with the major union: the opus release WITHIN the 4.x lines

mutation.description: a version is added to the release cut, so the generation narrowing and the release narrowing must both apply

provenance.ref: provider-qualified selector feeds the ordinary --provider machinery; claude-4.0 drops out because anthropic serves none of its entities, proving the qualification really filters. RE-MEASURED at the 2026-08-28 models.dev catalog refresh: `claude-4.1` now drops out TOO, for exactly the same reason claude-4.0 does — the anthropic provider stopped listing claude-opus-4-1, so it serves none of that line's entities even though 33 other providers still rehost them. The case gets stronger: two lines are now cascaded away by the qualification rather than one

mutation.description: a known-provider prefix is added, which must narrow the entities and cascade lines away, not be read as the family. Re-measured at the 2026-08-28 refresh: claude-4.1 joins claude-4.0 among the lines the qualification removes

provenance.ref: --version supplements a version-less selector on the canonical grammar too, so it is not a ladder-only flag

mutation.description: the version moves out of the canonical selector into --version; the result must equal claude/opus@4

provenance.ref: --input-format=canonical pins the grammar for scripting; a well-formed canonical selector resolves normally

mutation.description: the strict canonical format is requested for a selector that does parse as canonical

provenance.ref: a real models.dev catalog id; --input-format=models.dev resolves it through the ordinary lookup to its entity's line

mutation.description: the selector is a raw catalog id and the format says so, so only the id reading may fire

provenance.ref: infer precedence: ladder and canonical readings are tried and unioned first; the raw-id reading is the FINAL fallback and fires only when they find nothing

mutation.description: the same raw id is given with no --input-format, so the fallback rung must reach it

provenance.ref: --input-format=canonical promises NO fallback, so a raw id must fail loudly and point at the format that would read it

mutation.description: the raw-id case above is re-run under the strict canonical format, which must refuse the fallback that made it pass

provenance.ref: --input-format=models.dev reads ONLY raw ids, so a line rendering that resolves fine under infer must fail here

mutation.description: a selector that is a valid series rendering is re-run under the id-only format, which must not fall back to the ladder

provenance.ref: an unrecognized format value must name every member rather than silently defaulting to infer, which would give the caller the inference they were trying to avoid

mutation.description: the format value is misspelled, so the parse must reject rather than fall through to the default

provenance.ref: ruled: a canonical selector plus a --version that disagrees on version is an actionable error, not a silent precedence win

mutation.description: --version is set to a different version than the selector's @version, creating a contradiction that must surface

provenance.ref: ruled: an explicit --provider alongside a provider-qualified selector that disagrees is an actionable error

mutation.description: --provider names a different provider than the selector prefix, creating a contradiction that must surface

provenance.ref: a selector matching no reading at all stays the ordinary ErrNotFound, so adding readings never turned a miss into silence

mutation.description: the selector names nothing under any of the three readings, so every rung must miss and the generic not-found must be reported
